Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Saurabh Banerjee
 Order

The petitioners, vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, seek quashing of FIR No.0162/2013 dated 06.03.2013 registered under Section(s)
498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.: Kalyanpuri, East District, Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement dated 10.04.2023 arrived at between the parties at Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.
2.

This petition is accompanied by the Settlement dated 10.04.2023 and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
CRL.M.C. 8564/2023 page 1 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 18/12/2023 at 22:28:18 3.
Petitioner nos. 1 to 7 and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.

5. Learned APP for the State and learned counsel for the respondent no.2 accept notice.
6.
Learned APP for the State submits that since, this is a matrimonial dispute, he has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

sentences.text: 1 7. Respondent no.2 affirms the Settlement dated 10.04.2023 in respect of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

8. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.

9. Accordingly, the present petition is allowed and FIR No.0162/2013 dated 06.03.2013 registered under Section(s) 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.: Kalyanpuri, East District,
Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.

Needless to state that the settlement arrived at between the parties resulting in closure of all criminal proceedings inter se the parties by way of the present order will, in no way, effect the rights of the children of the late Sh. Sarjeet and the respondent no.2 namely Vipin and Vanshika vis-a- vis their parents, as may be available under law, in any manner whatsoever.
11. Accordingly, the present petition, alongwith the pending applications, if any, stands disposed of.
